record.question:
A document-sharing application runs on EC2 and stores PDFs in a private S3 bucket. After checking the signed-in user's authorization, the application checks whether a requested download exists and generates a presigned URL. Uploads also use presigned URLs. Long-term AWS access keys must not be stored on the instance.

Which configuration meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an IAM user with GetObject and PutObject permissions and store its access keys in an encrypted configuration file on the instance.
Create an IAM user with GetObject and PutObject permissions and associate the user with the instance so that its credentials appear in instance metadata.
Attach a role with ListBucket permission to the instance and read its temporary credentials from EC2 user data before signing URLs.

Attach an instance profile containing a role with GetObject and PutObject permissions on the permitted prefixes. Add ListBucket only if needed. Use the SDK's instance-profile credential provider with IMDSv2 to sign URLs.

explanation.text:
<<4>> is correct. The instance profile supplies a role to EC2, and the SDK obtains rotating temporary credentials from instance metadata. GetObject authorizes downloads and HeadObject checks, while PutObject authorizes uploads. Presigning runs locally with the credentials; S3 evaluates the resulting request against the signer's permissions. The application must authorize the user before issuing the URL.

<<1>> encrypts stored keys but still retains long-term credentials. <<2>> confuses an IAM user with an instance profile: EC2 metadata does not expose an attached IAM user's credentials. <<3>> lacks object read/write permissions and uses the wrong credential location; user data is not the instance-profile credential endpoint.

ListBucket is not needed simply to issue HeadObject, but it affects a missing object's response: 404 with ListBucket and 403 without it. A presigned URL is a bearer token and cannot remain valid beyond the signing credentials' lifetime. SSE-KMS objects can require additional KMS permissions.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/iam-roles-for-amazon-ec2.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_HeadObject.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-presigned-url.html

diagram_alt: The application performs authorization and signs locally, while the client transfers the PDF directly from S3.

sources.supports: Instance profiles deliver temporary role credentials to EC2 applications.
HeadObject needs GetObject and missing-object errors depend on ListBucket.
Presigned requests depend on signer permissions and temporary credential expiration.

editorial_notes: Preserved corrected GetObject and PutObject permissions and added the HeadObject 403-versus-404 qualification.
Removed instance sizing as irrelevant to credential selection.
